rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā conveys figurative elevation meaning firm establishment or mastery, as in the cited description of guidance.
rows.anchor: وحرف { على } للاستعلاء المجازي المراد به التمكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reassures the Messenger that he has not strayed at all from his commission and steadies believers in their faith.
rows.anchor: وهذا تثبيت للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وثناء عليه بأنه ما زاغ قيد أنملة عما بعثه الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause is counted as a sixth praise of the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وهذا أيضا ثناء سادس على القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being on a straight path is the reason for the command to hold fast and expresses the Messenger’s share of praise and support.
rows.anchor: المجعول علة للأمر بالثبات عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is praise and benefit, honoring the Messenger and his people; its followers gain guidance and benefit, while those who reject it are threatened with questioning.
rows.anchor: من إرادة أن هذا الدين يكسبه ويكسب قومه حسن السمعة في الأمم فمن اتبعه نال حظه من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word dhikr may mean intellectual recollection: guidance to what one did not know, like recalling something forgotten; many explain it as admonition.
rows.anchor: فشبه بتذكر الشيء المنسي وهو ما فسر به كثير الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dhikr means public mention: this religion gives the Messenger and his people an honored reputation among nations.
rows.anchor: والذكر بهذا المعنى غالب في الذكر بخبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr compares the verse’s ten meanings in a line’s space with Imruʾ al-Qays’s celebrated concise line, which has six; the verse adds emphasis, allusion, and verbal ornament.
rows.anchor: قفا نبكك من ذكرى حبيبب ومنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the punishment was lifted in response to Moses, Pharaoh and his chiefs broke their promise to accept guidance.
rows.anchor: أي تفرع على تضرعهم ووعدهم بالاهتداء إذا كشف عنهم العذاب أنهم نكثوا الوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nakth literally means undoing a tightly twisted rope and figuratively means betraying a covenant; the wording recalls the people’s breaking their promise in al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: والنكث : نقض الحبل المبرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction here follows the same pattern as the earlier sentence about people laughing at the signs.
rows.anchor: والكلام على تركيب هذه الجملة مثل الكلام على قوله آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing his people would follow Moses and believe, Pharaoh announced his own greatness to secure obedience and conceal his appeal for the punishment to be lifted, so they would think its end accidental.
rows.anchor: خشي فرعون أن يتبع قومه دعوة موسى ويؤمنوا برسالته فأعلن في قومه تذكيرهم بعظمة نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is a raised voice, but attributing it to Pharaoh is a rational metaphor because he ordered heralds to announce important royal matters publicly.
rows.anchor: والنداء : رفع الصوت ، وإسناده إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passage in al-Ḥarīrī’s thirtieth maqāmah illustrates a herald announcing a formal contract.
rows.anchor: ووقع في المقامة الثلاثين للحريري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause beginning qāla explains nādā, and attributing the speech to Pharaoh uses the same rational metaphor as attributing the call to him.
rows.anchor: وجملة { قال } الخ مبينة لجملة { نادى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Pharaoh depicted in this narrative is identified as Merneptah II.
rows.anchor: وفرعون المحكي عنه في هذه القصة هو منفطاح الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivers are Nile branches and canals, each so large it resembles a river, though they all belong to the single Nile.
rows.anchor: فالأنهار : فروع النيل وترعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Pharaoh’s capital was Memphis, the demonstrative points to the Nile’s two great branches near Cairo, Damietta and Rosetta, forming the Delta.
rows.anchor: فإن كان مقر ملك فرعون هذا في مدينة منفيس فاسم الإشارة في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Memphis reading, one branch may have been called Tanis after the city in that region, which the sea later submerged.
rows.anchor: وأحسب أنه الذي كان يدعى فرع تنيس لأن تنيس كانت في تلك الجهة وغمرها البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the capital was Thebes near present-day Abu, the demonstrative instead refers to the Nile’s familiar channels and branches visible to local residents.
rows.anchor: وإن كان مقر ملكه طيبة التي هي بقرب مدينة آبو اليوم فالإشارة إلى جداول النيل وفروعه المشهورة بين أهل المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of beneath me is that the Nile flows at Pharaoh’s command, with beneath serving as a metonym for subjugation, as in the cited phrase about two wives.
rows.anchor: أن النيل يجري بأمره ، فيكون { من تحتي } كناية عن التسخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Nile flows within his kingdom from Aswan to the sea, and beneath metaphorically expresses his control of its course, as on a river reading of the cited verse.
rows.anchor: أراد أن النيل يجري في مملكته من بلاد أصوان إلى البحر فيكون في { تحتي } استعارة للتمكن من تصاريف النيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such a boast could persuade the common people because their understanding was unsophisticated.
rows.anchor: وكان مثل هذا الكلام يروج على الدهماء لسذاجة عقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading takes the rivers as water outlets supplying the city and gardens, distributed by Pharaoh through dams and reservoirs; he boasts he could cut the water off, like Joseph’s claim about giving full measure.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالأنهار مصب المياه التي كانت تسقي المدينة والبساتين التي حولها وأن توزيع المياه كان بأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, beneath me means beneath my authority: the water flows only by his order.
rows.anchor: فيكون معنى { من تحتي } من تحت أمري أي لا تجري إلا بأمري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also reported that the rivers ran beneath Pharaoh’s palace.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل : كانت الأنهار تجري تحت قصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “Do you not see?” is an affirmative rhetorical prompt framed as a negative so the audience is pressed to acknowledge what they see.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام في { أفلا تبصرون } تقريري جاء التقرير على النفي تحقيقا لإقرارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause about the Hour is fronted for emphasis and to draw attention to the coming description of its conditions.
rows.anchor: وقدم عليه للاهتمام به واسترعاء الأسماع لما يرد من وصف أحواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawmaʾidh repeats the Hour’s time reference, with its tanwīn replacing an omitted genitive; the repetition confirms the report and heightens the dread of that day.
rows.anchor: وتنوينه عوض عن المضاف إليه المحذوف لدلالة ما أضيف إليه يوم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in tarā is general to any Qurʾānic addressee, though it may specifically address the Messenger; its present form points to the future.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في { ترى } لكل من يصلح له الخطاب بالقرآن فلا يقصد مخاطب معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ummah is a large group of people united by a religion brought to them by a messenger.
rows.anchor: والأمة : الجماعة العظيمة من الناس الذين يجمعهم دين جاء به رسول إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāthiyah describes a person kneeling in readiness, without resting the buttocks on the ground, a posture of submission.
rows.anchor: فالجاثي هو البارك المستوفز وهو هيئة الخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because kitābah is singular and indefinite, the apparent referent is each nation’s one scripture or law book, not individual deeds; it is summoned so its people’s deeds can be judged against its commands.
rows.anchor: أنه كتاب واحد لكل أمة فيقتضي أن يراد كتاب الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may instead refer to each person’s record of deeds, either distributively under a generic book or as an individual register.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أريد بقوله : { كتابها } كتاب تسجيل الأعمال لكل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the individual-record interpretation, Ibn ʿĀshūr cites the command to read one’s book and the criminals’ fear of the record; al-Kahf uses a definite book and thus makes its generality explicit.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended nations are those sent messengers with books and laws, consistent with the rule that God does not punish until a messenger is sent.
rows.anchor: فالمراد : خصوص الأمم التي أرسلت إليها الرسل ولها كتب وشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question of holding nations without messengers liable specifically for denying God or associating partners is treated in theological principles and was discussed under the cited rule.
rows.anchor: ومسألة مؤاخذة الأمم التي لم تجئها الرسل بخصوص جحد الإلاه أو الإشراكك به مقررة في أصول الدين

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read kullu as nominative, a subject whose predicate is tudʿā; the sentence resumes the discourse to answer why the nations are kneeling.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { كل أمة تدعى إلى كتابها } برفع { كل } على أنه مبتدأ و { تدعى } خبر عنه

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads kull as accusative, in apposition to the first kullu ummah, with tudʿā as a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: وقرأه يعقوب بنصب { كل } على البدل من قوله : { وترى كل أمة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating every nation rather than using a pronoun intensifies the scene: after kneeling, each nation is summoned and goes to judgment; a single combined clause could imply simultaneous kneeling and summons.
rows.anchor: فأعيدت كلمة { كل أمة } دون اكتفاء بقوله { تدعى } أو يدعون للتهويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Today you are recompensed is an explanatory apposition to being summoned, with an implied they are told; recompense matches deeds and the standards of their religious book.
rows.anchor: بدل اشتمال من جملة { تدعى إلى كتابها } بتقدير قول محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration this is Our Book is an implied utterance introduced to answer how the deeds are established; the book may be the nation’s scripture.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إما إلى كتاب شريعة الأمة المدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this Book refers to the individual records of deeds, construing the singular as a generic collective.
rows.anchor: وإما إلى كتب أفرادها على تأويل الكتاب بالجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the latter reading, the singular verb yantiqu matches the grammatical singular kitābunā, though the sense is that the books speak.
rows.anchor: وإفراد ضمير { ينطق } على هذا الوجه مراعاة للفظ { كتابنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Book is related to the nation because it records their deeds or contains their obligations, and to God because He commanded it.
rows.anchor: فالكتاب يلابس الأمة لأنه جعل لإحصاء أعمالهم أو لأن ما كلفوا به مثبت فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascribing speech to the Book is a rational metaphor: the accounting angels speak its contents.
rows.anchor: وإسناد النطق إلى الكتاب مجاز عقلي وإنما تنطق بما في الكتاب ملائكة الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, speaking is a metaphor for indicating or evidencing, as in the expression that a situation speaks.
rows.anchor: أو استعير النطق للدلالة نحو قولهم : نطقت الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book testifies either that deeds violated the scripture’s instructions or that they were recorded in individual registers, depending on which book is meant.
rows.anchor: أن فيه شهادة عليهم بأن أعمالهم مخالفة لوصايا الكتاب أو بأنها مكتوبة في صحائف أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yantiqu carries the sense of testifying, which accounts for its construction with the preposition ʿalā.
rows.anchor: ولتضمن { ينطق } معنى ( يشهد ) عدي بحرف ( على )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the passage threatens, it uses ʿalā alone and omits an added phrase meaning for you, emphasizing the threat.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المقام للتهديد اقتصر فيه على تعدية { ينطق } بحرف ( على ) دون زيادة : ولكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about copying is an explanatory answer to how the Book can testify now about past deeds: God had the deeds copied into records as they were done.
rows.anchor: فأجيبوا بأن الله كان يأمر بنسخ ما يعملونه في الصحف في وقت عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Book is scripture, the copying statement explains why its testimony is true: deeds were counted and those contrary to its commands identified.
rows.anchor: أي لأن أعمالكم كانت محصاة مبين ما هو منها مخالف لما أمر به كتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istinsākh is the derived tenth-form verbal noun of naskh.
rows.anchor: والاستنساخ : استفعال من النسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One lexical account treats naskh as copying a text after an earlier written model, also called muʿāraḍah; on the apparent meaning of al-Asās, saying the sun erased the shade is figurative.
rows.anchor: والنسخ : يطلق على كتابة ما يكتب على مثالل مكتوبب آخر قبله

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: The majority of scholars differ from that apparent lexical account, as reflected in legal theorists’ treatment of abrogation; al-Rāghib’s wording can support either usage.
rows.anchor: وكلام جمهور العلماء بخلافه كما يقوله علماء أصول الفقه في باب النسخ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās argues that, in Arabic, naskh must be copying from a book.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه يقول : ألستم عربا وهل يكون النسخ إلا من كتاب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s al-Asās explicitly treats writing without copying an earlier text as a literal sense of naskh, and al-Kashshāf appears to do so too, making the word polysemous.
rows.anchor: كلام الزمخشري في الأساس صريح في أنه من معاني النسخ حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the lexicographers of Lisān and al-Qāmūs: transferring writing is called naskh only when modeled on earlier writing; general writing may be the root sense.
rows.anchor: والأظهر ما ذهب إليه صاحب ( اللسان ) وصاحب ( القاموس )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sīn and tāʾ in نستنسخ may intensify the action, as in istajāba beside ajāba.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون السين والتاء في { نستنسخ } للمبالغة في الفعل مثل استجاب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Alternatively, the sīn and tāʾ express requesting or commissioning: the commentators understand God to task the angels with copying the deeds.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا المحمل حمل المفسرون السين والتاء هنا أي للطلب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On the commissioned-copying reading, Ibn ʿAbbās says God assigns angels during Ramadan to copy from the Mother of the Book all human deeds that will occur.
rows.anchor: وبه فسر ابن عباس قال : إن الله وكل ملائكة ينسخون من أم الكتاب في رمضان كل ما سيكون من أعمال بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that naskh means recording what people do without copying it from a prior original.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون النسخ بمعنى كتابة ما تعلمه الناس دون نقل عن أصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istʿitāb means iʿtāb, with sīn and tāʾ intensifying the action as in istajāba; it is granting satisfaction, and here the passive says no one will appease them or grant what they ask.
rows.anchor: والاستعتاب بمعنى : الإعتاب ، فالسين والتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting hum before the verb hints that God will satisfy others, namely forgive the believers.
rows.anchor: تقديم { هم } على { يستعتبون } وهو مسند فعلي بعد حرف النفي هنا تعريض بأن الله يعتب غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa grounds praise in the surah’s account of God’s favors in creation, guidance, subjugation, justice, and blessings to Muslims, along with warnings and arguments against rejecters; thus He deserves exclusive praise.
rows.anchor: الفاء لتفريع التحميد والثناء على الله تفريعا على ما احتوت عليه السورة من ألطاف الله فيما خلق وأرشد وسخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement can be a plain report that praise belongs to God, an indirect command that people reserve praise for Him, or praise and celebration offered to Him; all prior verses suit these readings.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون هذا الكلام مرادا منه ظاهر الإخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting li-llāh signals exclusivity: true and complete praise belongs to God alone, as explained in the opening sūrah.
rows.anchor: وتقديم ( لله ) لإفادة الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Him Lord of the heavens explains and reinforces His exclusive claim to praise; repeating Lord for earth honors His lordship over both realms and their inhabitants’ duty to praise Him.
rows.anchor: وإجراء وصف رب السماوات } على اسمه تعالى إيماء إلى علة قصر الحمد على الله إخبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lord of the worlds further establishes that heaven and earth’s inhabitants owe God praise, because He created both the worlds from which they benefit and their very selves.
rows.anchor: لأنه خالق العوالم التي هم منتفون بها وخالق ذواتهم فيها كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s possession of majesty shows that calling creation to praise benefits and purifies them; He Himself needs nothing from them, as the cited verses state.
rows.anchor: للإشارة إلى أن استدعاءه خلقه لحمده إنما هو لنفعهم وتزكية نفوسهم فإنه غني عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the phrase unto Him is like fronting unto God in the preceding verse and signals exclusivity.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المجرور في { وله الكبرياء } مثله في { فلله الحمد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kibriyāʾ is true greatness: perfection of attributes and of existence.
rows.anchor: والكبرياء : الكبر الحق الذي هو كمال الصفات وكمال الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz gathers power and freedom of choice, while al-Ḥakīm gathers complete and universal knowledge; the closing wording signals the sūrah’s end with an artful finale.
rows.anchor: لأن العزة تشمل معاني القدرة والاختيار ، والحكمة تجمع معاني تمام العلم وعمومه

none: Bare heading and Qurʾānic text only; no commentary point is present.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God to inspire the speaker and include his parents, so personal supplication does not crowd out prayer for them; their direct kindness is already implied by the argument from forbidding even a mild rebuke.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يشغله الدعاء لنفسه عن الدعاء لهما وبأنه يحسن إليهما بظهر الغيب منهما حين مناجاته ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands kindness to parents both in their presence and absence, through every means that benefits them, as in the prayer to show them mercy as they raised the child.
rows.anchor: أن الله أمر بالإحسان إلى الوالدين في المشاهدة والغيبة وبجميع وسائل الإحسان الذي غايته حصول النفع لهما

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a person’s deeds end at death except for ongoing charity, knowledge imparted, and a righteous child who prays for the deceased parent; the author uses it to support the prayer for parents.
rows.anchor: إذا مات ابن آدم انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a child thanks God for blessings bestowed on the parents, the child acts on their behalf and performs a good deed for them.
rows.anchor: وما شكر الولد ربه على النعمة التي أنعمها الله على والديه إلا من باب نيابته عنهما في هذا الشكر

rows.speaker: الفضل بن عباس
rows.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage, a Khathʿamī woman asked whether she could perform Hajj for her elderly father, who could not remain on a mount; the Prophet answered yes.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث الفضل بن عباس أن المرأة الخثعمية قالت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم حجة الوداع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hajj done for the father was not an obligatory Hajj for him because incapacity prevented him from performing it.
rows.anchor: وهو حج غير واجب على أبيها لعجزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd denotes the strengthening of mental and physical faculties; it is a plural with no attested singular.
rows.anchor: والأشد : حالة اشتداد القوى العقلية والجسدية وهو جمع لم يسمع له بمفرد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed linguistic opinion treats shiddah, with a feminine ending, as the singular of ashudd, by analogy with niʿmah and anʿum.
rows.anchor: وقيل مفرده : شدة بكسر الشين وهاء التأنيث مثل نعمة جمعها أنعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd does not denote a fixed number of years: age is only its likely setting; it begins after thirty and reaches completion at forty, so forty marks full maturity rather than a redundant restatement.
rows.anchor: ووقته ما بعد الثلاثين سنة وتمامه عند الأربعين سنة ولذلك عطف على { بلغ أشده } قوله : { وبلغ أربعين سنة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awziʿnī means inspire me; the root denotes removing restraint, with the hamza causative of removal.
rows.anchor: و { أوزعني } : ألهمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Niʿmataka is a verbal noun used inclusively: the prayer asks gratitude for every religious blessing, such as faith and guidance, and worldly blessing, such as health and wealth, given to the speaker and his parents.
rows.anchor: أي ألهمني شكر النعم التي أنعمت بها علي وعلى والدي من جميع النعم الدينية كالإيمان والتوفيق ومن النعم الدنيوية كالصحة والجدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request to reform descendants is an aside within the prayer for parents, directing one to attend to future generations as well; their reform includes inspiring them to pray for their parent.
rows.anchor: استطراد في أثناء الوصاية بالدعاء للوالدين بأن لا يغفل الإنسان عن التفكر في مستقبله بأن يصرف عنايته إلى ذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Including descendants hints that a person may receive the same kindness from children that the person gave parents, and that a parent’s prayer for a child is likely answered.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى أن المرء يلقى من إحسان أبنائه إليه مثل ما لقي أبواه من إحسانه إليهما

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayrah reports from the Prophet that three prayers are answered without doubt; the wording has a variant for a parent’s prayer against a child versus for a child, and the author grades the report ḥasan with multiple routes.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ثلاث دعوات مستجابات لا شك فيهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li of wa-aṣliḥ lī is causal: reform the descendants for my sake and benefit, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: واللام في { وأصلح لي } لام العلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding this request seeks divine grace after recalling blessings on the speaker and parents; it lays out a progression toward the response: complete the favor by reforming the descendants for his benefit.
rows.anchor: وهذه ترقيات بديعة في درجات القرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ظرفية in fī dhurriyyatī makes descendants a container in which reform settles, conveying that it becomes firmly established and permeates them.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ظرفية { في ذريتي } أن ذريته نزلت منزلة الظرف يستقر فيه ما هو به الإصلاح
